newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strauss-Kahn against rigid EMU criteria reading.
newsitem.headline: Strauss-Kahn against rigid EMU criteria reading.

text.p: French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said on Tuesday he was against a purely "accounting-style" reading of the Maastricht entry criteria for the European single currency.

Speaking from Amsterdam, he told French radio the essential point was that countries preparing for monetary union should be on the way to meeting the target for budget deficit to GDP of three percent.
"I think, as we have always said, the most important thing is to be approaching three percent, what we call trending towards three percent," Strauss-Kahn told Europe 1 radio.
"That means countries should be approaching three percent and show that they are on trend towards reducing to three percent, even if they have not reached it," he said.
"Not everyone shares that interpretation of the treaty, but I think we must argue for this because we do not want a purely accounting-style type of reasoning," he said.

France's Socialist party, which leads the broad-left government elected on June 1, supports European monetary union but said during the election campaign it would oppose fresh austerity needed to meet a strict reading of the Maastricht criteria.
